Rashi on Shabbat 140a:10:1.english: And I felt [it] from the hair of the head - I felt its chill from the hair of my head to the nails of my feet.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:10:2.english: They would deduct from my merits - If I were saved from it so that I would not die.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:10:3.english: [He] drank every day - And it did not harm him.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:10:4.english: As he grew accustomed to it - [He was] accustomed to it.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:11:1.hebrew: חילתית - חלטי"ש בלשון ישמעאל ובלע"ז לזרי"א, ושורין אותו בפושרין ושותין אותן המים לרפואה:
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:11:1.english: Chiltit [Asafoetida] - [It is called] chaltish in the language of Ishmael [Arabic], and in the vernacular [Old French] lazere [laserwort]; and they soak it in lukewarm water and drink that water for healing.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:11:2.english: However, one may place - the asafoetida.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:11:3.hebrew: בתוך החומץ - ומטבל בו מאכלו, ולקמיה מפרש אמאי אין שורין:
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:11:3.english: Into vinegar - And he dips his food in it, and later on [the Gemara] explains why one may not soak [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:11:4.hebrew: ואין שולין את הכרשינין - מציף עליהם מים בכלי לברור פסולתן, כדתנן במסכת ביצה (דף יד:): אף מדיח ושולה:
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:11:4.english: And one may not soak [lit., float] the vetches - [That is, one] floats water over them in a vessel to separate their refuse, as we learned in a Mishnah in tractate Beitzah (14b): "[One may] even rinse and float [them]."

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:11:5.hebrew: ולא שפין אותן - ביד להסיר פסולת, דהוה ליה בורר:
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:11:5.english: Nor rub them - By hand, to remove [the] refuse, for it is [considered] selecting.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:11:6.hebrew: אבל נותן לתוך הכברה - ואע"פ דפעמים שהפסולת נופל דרך נקבי הכברה, ונמצא נתברר מאליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:11:6.english: However, one may place [them] into a sieve - Even though sometimes the waste falls through the holes of the sieve, and it turns out [to be] sifted on its own.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:12:1.hebrew: תבן - הוא שעושין מן הקש; מחתכין אותו במוריגין, ועושה כל זנב השבולת תבן:
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:12:1.english: Straw - This is what is made from stubble; they chop it with threshing sledges, and it makes the entire tail of the ear of grain into straw.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:12:2.hebrew: מוץ - הוא מזקן השבולת העליון, ואינו ראוי למאכל, וכוברין אותו בכברין שיפול המוץ:
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:12:2.english: Chaff - It is from the upper beard of the ear of grain, and it is not fit for food, and they sift it [the straw] in sieves so that the chaff will fall [out].

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:12:3.hebrew: אבל נוטל בכברה - ליתן בתוך האבוס, ואע"פ שהמוץ נופל מאליו, כר"ש דאמר דבר שאין מתכוין מותר:
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:12:3.english: However, one may take [it] in a sieve - to place [it] into the trough, and even though the chaff falls out on its own, [this is] in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, who says [that] an unintended act is permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:13:1.english: [If] one soaked - asafoetida in lukewarm water, what [is the law]?

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:14:2.english: So that he will not do, etc. - The Rabbis did not allow him to perform weekday activities.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:16:1.hebrew: אם כן - דלא ידענא לפרושי מתני' טפי מינך, מה בין לי ולך:
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:16:1.english: If so - that I do not know how to explain the Mishnah better than you, what is [the difference] between me and you?

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:16:2.hebrew: מתניתין יחידאה היא - ור' יוסי אמרה, אבל לרבנן אף בצונן אסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:16:2.english: Our Mishnah is [the opinion of] an individual - And Rabbi Yosei stated it, whereas according to the Rabbis, even in cold [water] it is prohibited.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:17:1.english: For heaviness of the heart - That his heart is heavy upon him.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:17:2.hebrew: תלתא תקלי חילתתא - משקל ג' זהובים:
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:17:2.english: Three shekels of asafoetida - The weight of three gold coins.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:17:3.english: He asked in the study hall - what he should do on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:18:1.hebrew: לשתות לא קמיבעיא לי - דבלאו רפואה משקה הוא, ותנן: כל המשקין שותה (לעיל שבת דף קט:):
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:18:1.english: With regard to drinking, I have no dilemma - For even without [its use as] a remedy, it is a beverage, and we learned in a Mishnah: "One may drink all beverages" (above, Shabbat 109b).

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:18:2.english: To soak - For we learned in our Mishnah: One may not soak [asafoetida].

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:19:1.hebrew: כמאן דשרי - בעיא הוא: הך דרב, לימא כרבי יוסי דשרי בצונן, אבל לרבנן אסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:19:1.english: According to the one who permits - It is a question: [Regarding] this [ruling] of Rav, shall we say [it is] according to Rabbi Yosei, who permits [soaking asafoetida] in cold [water], whereas according to the Rabbis it is prohibited?

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:1:1.hebrew: לפי שאין עושין אלא לגוון - למראה, שהחלמון יפה לגוון ולא החלבון. הלכך, אידי ואידי אוכל הוא, ואין כאן ברירת פסולת מאוכל:
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:1:1.english: Because it is only made for color - For appearance, since the yolk is good for color, and not the white. Therefore, both this and that are food, and there is no selecting of waste from food here.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:20:1.english: Ayyileina - Bring me in, and he was an old man.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:20:2.hebrew: לכסכוסי כיתניתא - חלוק, כתונת של פשתן שנתכבסה והרי היא קשה, ומשפשפה בין שתי ידיו והיא מתרככה, ואף הליבון שלה מצהיל על ידי השפשוף:
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:20:2.english: To rub a linen shirt - A shirt, a linen tunic that was laundered and is [now] stiff, and one rubs it between his two hands and it softens, and its whiteness also brightens through the rubbing.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:23:2.hebrew: התם מיחזי כאולודי חיורא - שמקפיד על ליבונו וצוהרו של סודר יותר מכיתניתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:23:2.english: There it appears like generating whiteness - For one is more particular about the whiteness and brightness of a scarf than [that] of a linen shirt.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:2:1.hebrew: ממחו - דישטיפדי"ר בלע"ז, במים או ביין:
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:2:1.english: One may dissolve it - "Destemprer" in Old French [to dissolve], in water or in wine.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:2:2.english: One may dissolve it with a vessel - [This] implies [that] this is its deviation.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:2:3.english: And one does not dissolve it by hand - Because one dissolves it much better [that way].

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:3:1.english: Rather, Shmuel said: He may dissolve it by hand - For this is not its [usual] manner on a weekday.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:5:1.hebrew: קם ר' יוחנן בשיטתיה דר"א - חזר בו ואסר:
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:5:1.english: Rabbi Yochanan stood in the opinion of Rabbi Elazar - He retracted [his earlier view] and prohibited [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:5:2.hebrew: אביי ורבא דאמרי תרוייהו הלכה כר' יוחנן - דאסר:
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:5:2.english: Abaye and Rava both said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan - Who prohibits [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:6:2.english: With the inner part of the garlic - The middle [part] of the garlic.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:7:1.hebrew: ולא יטרוף - כדרך שטורפין ביצים בקערה בכף, דרך טריפה שמכה בכח:
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:7:1.english: And he may not beat [it] - Like the way one beats eggs in a bowl with a spoon, [which is] a manner of beating where one strikes forcefully.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:8:1.hebrew: שחליים - כרישין, והיו שוחקין אותם במים:
Rashi on Shabbat 140a:8:1.english: Cress - Leeks, and they would grind them in water.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:8:4.english: Is beneficial for taḥlei - To mix with cress.

Rashi on Shabbat 140a:9:1.english: And one may not prepare aluntit - For it is not [meant] as a drink for thirst, but rather to cool [oneself] after the bathhouse, and [it is] akin to a remedy.
